stories.title: CBRE Arranges Sale of Boutique Bergen County Apartments
stories.excerpt: A CBRE team led by Jeffrey Dunne, Stuart MacKenzie, Eric Apfel, Travis Langer and Eric Greenberg of CBRE Institutional Properties, in partnership with Charles Berger of CBRE Investment Properties, closed the sale of Lexington Riverview, a Class A multifamily property located in the Bergen County community of Fair Lawn, NJ, for $14.9 million. CBRE represented the seller while David Ferber with Matthews represented the buyer. Completed in 2021, Lexington Riverview is a boutique luxury apartment community consisting of 43 market-rate apartments. The property is situated along the Passaic River, offering waterfront views, while only a mile away from NJ Transit’s Radburn Train Station, providing daily access to New York in approximately 45 minutes. “We generated significant interest in the asset by combining CBRE’s institutional and private capital platforms,” said Berger. “We’re thrilled with the outcome, especially given the challenges in today’s market driven by interest rate volatility.” The post CBRE Arranges Sale of Boutique Bergen County Apartments appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: CBRE closed $14.9M sale of Lexington Riverview, 43-unit Class A in Fair Lawn, NJ
2021-built boutique property near NJ Transit Radburn station, 45-min commute to NYC
Sale reflects strong institutional capital appetite despite interest rate volatility headwinds
stories.summary: CBRE arranged the sale of Lexington Riverview, a 43-unit luxury apartment community completed in 2021 in Fair Lawn, Bergen County, NJ, for $14.9 million. The property benefits from waterfront access along the Passaic River and proximity to NJ Transit's Radburn Train Station, offering a 45-minute commute to Manhattan. Despite market challenges driven by interest rate volatility, CBRE's combined institutional and private capital platforms generated significant buyer interest.
stories.impact: Transit-proximate Bergen County submarkets with NYC connectivity remain attractive to multifamily capital even in a higher-rate environment. The deal signals demand for well-located, recently-built rental product in the New Jersey suburbs serving New York workers—an important indicator for acquisition and development pipeline strategy in the Northern NJ corridor.

stories.title: Kirkland Condominium Project Reaches Construction Milestone
stories.excerpt: Cordillera Homes announced several significant construction milestones at Central Peak Residences, a boutique collection of 26 condominiums in the heart of downtown Kirkland, including completion of the project’s cast-in-place concrete structure and the start of wood framing. “This is an exciting point in the construction of Central Peak Residences, when people can start to see the community we’ve envisioned coming to life,” said Nick Tosti, principal at Cordillera Homes. The community will comprise just 26 single-level residences ranging from approximately 1,150 to 2,415 square feet. Designed in collaboration with Baylis Architects, the four-story building will include a neighborhood café, a lounge, secure bike storage, dedicated below-grade parking, and a rooftop terrace. Its location places residents in the heart of downtown Kirkland, just steps from Marina Park, Kirkland Urban, the Cross-Kirkland Corridor and the Lake Washington waterfront. Project partners include Baylis Architects, Brumbaugh and Associates, Encompass Engineering & Surveying, and DCI Structural Engineering. The post Kirkland Condominium Project Reaches Construction Milestone appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Cordillera Homes advances Central Peak Residences, 26-unit condo in downtown Kirkland, WA
Four-story mixed-use project with café, rooftop terrace, near Marina Park and waterfront
Concrete structure complete, wood framing underway; on-track delivery signals strong local demand
stories.summary: Cordillera Homes announced construction milestones at Central Peak Residences, a boutique 26-unit condominium project in downtown Kirkland, Washington. The four-story building is completing its cast-in-place concrete structure and beginning wood framing, with amenities including a neighborhood café, lounge, bike storage, and rooftop terrace. Units range from 1,150 to 2,415 square feet and are steps from Marina Park, Lake Washington, and the Cross-Kirkland Corridor.
stories.impact: This is a condo project, not rental; limited relevance to apartment development. However, Kirkland's waterfront downtown infill activity and pace of delivery reflect sustained demand for mixed-use residential in Pacific Northwest transit-oriented communities, which may indicate favorable rents and occupancy in nearby multifamily assets.

stories.title: Buyer Moves Fast to Acquire Southern New Hampshire Industrial
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap closed the sale of an industrial property in Hudson, NH, near the Massachusetts border. The asset sold for $3.9 million. “We ran a targeted process to a short list of buyers who could actually perform, and that’s what got this to the finish line,” said Luigi Lessa, director investments in Marcus & Millichap’s Boston office. “Southern New Hampshire industrial is still trading because the demand is real and the supply isn’t. The buyer moved quickly, stayed at the table through a complicated closing, and we kept both sides focused on getting it done.” The Lessa Edenkrans Group of Marcus & Millichap, in association with Thomas Shihadeh, the firm’s broker of record in New Hampshire, marketed the property on behalf of seller Dan Lang and procured the buyer, V12 Investments. The property, located at 32 Executive Drive, is a 36,800-square-foot high-bay industrial warehouse on a 4.58-acre lot. The single-story property was built in 1973 and is divisible into two units, offering potential for multi-tenant use. The post Buyer Moves Fast to Acquire Southern New Hampshire Industrial appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Marcus & Millichap sold 36,800-sq-ft industrial warehouse in Hudson, NH for $3.9M
Broker noted strong demand and supply shortage in Southern New Hampshire industrial sector
Quick buyer performance (V12 Investments) underscores competitive, tight market conditions
stories.summary: Marcus & Millichap closed the sale of a 36,800-square-foot high-bay industrial warehouse at 32 Executive Drive in Hudson, NH (near Massachusetts border) for $3.9 million. The single-story 1973-built property on 4.58 acres is divisible into two units. Broker Luigi Lessa noted that Southern New Hampshire industrial remains in tight supply relative to demand, with the buyer moving quickly despite closing complexity.
stories.impact: Not directly relevant to multifamily development. However, tight industrial supply and strong buyer competition in Southern NH signals regional economic vitality and logistics hub strength near Boston, which supports job creation and population retention in the corridor—indirect tailwinds for multifamily rental demand in the Boston metro exurban markets.

stories.title: Michaels Organization Set to Break Ground in Davis
stories.excerpt: The Michaels Organization, a national leader in residential real estate, and its partners, Kyuden Urban Development America and Japan Overseas Infrastructure Investment Corporation for Transport & Urban Development (JOIN), are poised to break ground on a new multifamily housing community featuring ground-floor commercial space in Davis. The $88-million development, branded “The Lumberyard,” will rise on the former site of Hibbert’s Lumberyard and Hardware Store at the intersection of G and 5th Streets in downtown Davis. The five-story mid-rise will offer 239 apartments, 5% of which will be set aside for households earning 50% or less of the Area Median Income. This is Michaels’ first partnership with Kyuden Urban Development America and  JOIN USA. “We are excited and thankful for the opportunity to partner with Kyuden and JOIN on this transformative development,” said Michael Flannagan, Michaels’ CIO. “Working alongside their teams to reach this financial closing has been a wonderful experience, and we are thrilled to officially break ground and begin the journey of bringing The Lumberyard to life alongside such dedicated partners.” The post Michaels Organization Set to Break Ground in Davis appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Michaels Organization breaks ground on The Lumberyard, 239-unit mid-rise in downtown Davis, CA
$88M development on former Hibbert's Lumberyard site, 5% AMI-restricted units included
First partnership with Kyuden Urban Development America and JOIN USA; foreign capital influx
stories.summary: The Michaels Organization and partners Kyuden Urban Development America and Japan Overseas Infrastructure Investment Corporation for Transport & Urban Development (JOIN) broke ground on The Lumberyard, an $88 million, five-story mixed-use development in downtown Davis, California. The project will deliver 239 apartments with 5% set-aside for households earning 50% AMI or less, plus ground-floor commercial space on the former site of Hibbert's Lumberyard at G and 5th Streets.
stories.impact: Davis's downtown infill redevelopment signals strong demand for student and young professional housing near UC Davis. Japanese capital entering the U.S. multifamily market through Kyuden/JOIN indicates international investor confidence in Sacramento Valley rents despite U.S. rate environment. This is a bellwether for Central Valley supply pipeline and reflects confidence in mid-size university towns' rental fundamentals.

stories.title: Gillette Acquires South Boston Site for $1B Technical Innovation Center
stories.excerpt: Life science real estate developer Breakthrough Properties has finalized the sale of its 232 A Street development site in South Boston to P&G Gillette, following Gillette’s previously announced plans to establish its new Grooming Headquarters and Technical Innovation Center at the site. Gillette plans to invest nearly $1 billion in the new facility. Breakthrough, a joint venture of Tishman Speyer and Bellco Capital, originally acquired the 2.4-acre site in 2021 for $80 million and subsequently secured approval for a 325,000-square-foot research and development campus with 1.5 acres of enhanced public realm, including a vibrant waterfront park on the Fort Point Channel. Founded in Boston approximately 125 years ago, Gillette paid approximately $99,285,703 for the site. The sale was facilitated by Jonathan Varholak of CBRE. “The sale of the fully approved 232 A Street development site to P&G Gillette underscores the enduring demand for best-in-class infill locations in the world’s leading innovation markets,” said Breakthrough Properties EVP and CIO Daniel D’Orazi. “We are proud of the thoughtful execution—from acquisition through design and entitlement—that positioned this prime waterfront site for its exciting next phase with P&G Gillette.” The post Gillette Acquires South Boston Site for $1B Technical Innovation Center appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: P&G Gillette acquired South Boston site from Breakthrough Properties for ~$99.3M
Gillette investing $1B in new Grooming HQ and R&D campus on 2.4-acre waterfront
Breakthrough paid $80M in 2021; $19M gain reflects site appreciation and entitlement value
stories.summary: Breakthrough Properties sold its fully-approved 232 A Street development site in South Boston to P&G Gillette for approximately $99.3 million. Gillette plans to invest nearly $1 billion in a new Grooming Headquarters and Technical Innovation Center on the 2.4-acre Fort Point Channel waterfront parcel. Breakthrough, a Tishman Speyer-Bellco Capital joint venture, acquired the site in 2021 for $80 million and secured approvals for a 325,000-square-foot R&D campus with enhanced public realm.
stories.impact: Gillette's major life-science/manufacturing investment in Boston signals sustained demand for innovation-district real estate and will drive demand for workforce housing in nearby submarkets. Fort Point and surrounding neighborhoods will see intensified white-collar job growth, supporting rental demand and pricing power in proximate multifamily assets. This validates Boston's appeal to legacy corporate R&D relocations.

stories.title: New York City’s Technology Labor Market Has Surpassed San Francisco: Report
stories.excerpt: It’s official. New York is employing more tech workers than the San Francisco Bay area. According to an annual CBRE report on North American tech talent, the New York metropolitan area’s tech workforce reached 394,300 in 2025. The stat marks an 8.4 percent increase from 2022 that added 30,640 jobs. Meanwhile, San Francisco’s tech employment fell by 6 percent over the same period, totaling 375,730 jobs in 2025. This is the first time in the report’s 13-year history that the Big Apple has come out ahead. The city’s diversified job market helped set it apart, Colin Yasukochi, executive director of CBRE’s tech insights center, told Commercial Observer. “What really pushed New York past the San Francisco Bay Area has been the job reductions that we’ve seen [in San Francisco], with a lot of the announced layoffs, and the fact that New York has continued to grow,” Yasukochi said. San Francisco remains in North America’s top spot for its pool of tech talent, however, ranked across 13 metrics. The report, which analyzed the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics and LinkedIn data, found that tech jobs make up more than 10 percent of total employment in San Francisco, compared to just 4.2 percent in New York. But a whopping 61 percent of San Francisco’s tech talent works directly in the tech industry, according to CBRE’s report, leaving its general labor market vulnerable. bullets: NYC metro tech workforce reached 394,300 in 2025, up 8.4% since 2022 (30,640 jobs added)
San Francisco tech employment fell 6% to 375,730; first time NYC has surpassed SF in 13-year report
NYC's job market diversity and SF's announced layoffs drove divergence between coasts
stories.summary: According to CBRE's annual North American tech talent report, the New York metropolitan area's tech workforce reached 394,300 in 2025, marking an 8.4 percent increase since 2022 that added 30,640 jobs. Meanwhile, San Francisco's tech employment declined 6 percent over the same period to 375,730 jobs. This is the first time in the report's 13-year history that New York has surpassed the Bay Area. CBRE's Colin Yasukochi attributed the shift to job reductions and announced layoffs in San Francisco and continued growth diversity in New York.
stories.impact: NYC's emergence as America's largest tech employment hub reshapes multifamily demand curves in the New York metro area, particularly in transit-proximate, high-amenity submarkets (Brooklyn, Long Island City, Manhattan, Westchester). Rising white-collar job concentration will sustain rental demand and rent growth momentum; developers should prioritize acquisitions and starts in neighborhoods with strong tech talent clustering and transit access (Midtown Manhattan, Hudson Yards, Astoria, Downtown Brooklyn, Jersey City PATH corridors).

stories.title: Principal Financial Group Loans $32M to Refi Queens Shopping Center
stories.excerpt: An affiliate of Mattone Investors secured $32 million to refinance Springnex Plaza, a 96,028-square-foot shopping center anchored by a Stop & Shop supermarket in the Queens neighborhood of Springfield Gardens. Principal Financial Group provided the debt, while Northmarq’s Robert Delitsky and Charles Cotsalas arranged the transaction. Delitsky noted in a statement that Mattone Investors first developed Springnex Plaza six years ago and “have done a fabulous job maintaining very strong occupancy” since then. “Supermarket-anchored shopping centers like Springnex Plaza will continue to attract very strong lender interest in today’s market,” Cotsalas added in the same statement. Located at 134-40 Springfield Boulevard, Springnex Plaza sits on 5.58 acres of land and is 100 percent occupied. Besides Stop & Shop, tenants include an IHOP, fashion retailer Ashley Stewart and Northwell Health GoHealth Urgent Care. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Mattone Investors refinanced Springnex Plaza, 96,028-sq-ft shopping center in Queens, for $32M
100% occupied Stop & Shop-anchored center in Springfield Gardens, full amenity tenant roster
Principal Financial Group lender; strong lender appetite for supermarket-anchored retail
stories.summary: An affiliate of Mattone Investors secured a $32 million refinancing from Principal Financial Group for Springnex Plaza, a 96,028-square-foot shopping center in the Springfield Gardens neighborhood of Queens, New York. The property sits on 5.58 acres and is 100 percent occupied, anchored by Stop & Shop and including IHOP, Ashley Stewart, and Northwell Health GoHealth Urgent Care. Mattone developed the center six years prior and has maintained strong occupancy since.
stories.impact: Not directly relevant to multifamily development. However, supermarket-anchored retail refinancing strength and full occupancy in Queens outer-borough neighborhoods indicate underlying economic stability and consumer resilience in density-constrained areas. This suggests neighboring multifamily assets in outer Queens submarkets (Springfield Gardens, Jamaica, Astoria) may benefit from sustained local tenant demand and neighborhood vitality, supporting rent retention.

stories.title: Data Center Development Has Domestic Materials Manufacturers Working Overtime
stories.excerpt: Development in the U.S. saw spotty progress in the first half of 2026 with costs of materials continuing to climb and asset classes with only the highest returns being built. That means data centers, power infrastructure, advanced manufacturing and pharmaceutical production are taking off, while office, retail and higher education on a national level lag way behind, due, in large part, to President Donald Trump’s ongoing tariff policies, according to a Skanska report. But just because there is a lull in some sectors does not mean supply chains for materials aren’t working at full capacity, Tom Park, vice president of national strategic supply chain at Skanska, told Commercial Observer. “The market is hot and cold right now — hot and warm may be a better way to say it — so what stands out is that we’re seeing a lot of project activity around data centers, semiconductor, life sciences,” Park said in an interview. “There’s really a lot of unprecedented demand in the mechanical, electrical, plumbing and steel space driving up lead times and cost.” Some factors causing these supply chain hemorrhages are Section 338 tariffs on Canada, delays on petrochemical import ships through the Strait of Hormuz, and domestic materials priced higher simply because of the supply and demand constraints. Tariffs on steel, aluminum and copper in particular are driving prices up. “What happens with tariffs is that it really raises the opportunity for domestic producers to raise their prices,” Park said. “For steel, aluminum and copper, the tariffs really have increased pricing on all those materials and derivative products because the foreign competition obviously has that tariff to overcome.” Lead times for material deliveries have increased from 24 to 36 weeks to 40 to 50 weeks, indicating to Park that metal mills and fabricators are running at full capacity. bullets: Trump tariff policies driving material cost inflation; data centers, advanced mfg, pharma booming
Office, retail, higher education construction lagging nationally due to ROI constraints and tariffs
Unprecedented demand in MEP and steel sector creating supply chain bottlenecks, extended lead times
stories.summary: According to a Skanska report, U.S. development in H1 2026 faced spotty progress with climbing material costs, with only asset classes offering the highest returns being built. Data centers, power infrastructure, advanced manufacturing, and pharmaceutical production are accelerating, while office, retail, and higher education lag nationally. Tom Park, VP of national strategic supply chain at Skanska, cited President Trump's ongoing tariff policies as a primary driver and noted unprecedented demand in mechanical, electrical, plumbing, and steel sectors is driving up lead times and costs.
stories.impact: Tariff-driven material inflation and extended MEP/steel lead times directly impact multifamily development feasibility and underwriting. Developers must expect elevated hard costs, longer procurement timelines, and potential schedule delays on any projects breaking ground in 2026–27. This will compress margins on new starts unless rents rise sharply; capital will shift toward stabilized acquisitions and value-add plays over ground-up development in lower-rent, cost-sensitive markets. Repricing of development yields is underway.

stories.title: Azora, Vizcaya Capital Flip Coconut Grove Office Building for $62M
stories.excerpt: Just a year after buying a boutique office building in Miami’s coveted Coconut Grove neighborhood, Azora Private Solutions and Vizcaya Capital sold it for a nearly $15 million gain. The five-story property at 3250 Mary Street, called the Grove at 3250 Mary, sold for $62.3 million, according to the brokers who represented the sellers, Berkadia’s Omar Morales and Jaret Turkell. The joint venture had purchased the 80,000-square-foot building for $47.5 million last September. Records show the buyer is an entity tied to El-Ad National Properties, the Boca Raton-based division of Israeli billionaire Isaac Tshuva’s El-Ad Group. “Coconut Grove continues to distinguish itself as one of South Florida’s strongest real estate markets, driven by exceptional demand from luxury residential buyers and high-net-worth office users,” Morales said in a statement. “That demand, combined with limited supply, continues to attract remarkable investment to the neighborhood.” In recent years, Coconut Grove has attracted a slew of billionaires, including Google’s billionaire founder Larry Page, who spent about $170 million assembling a residential compound last year. The residential acquisitions have fueled demand for luxury office space nearby. The acquisition of the 1982-built, 1.3-acre site office building marks somewhat of a deviation for El-Ad National, which has typically focused on residential and mixed-use development. It also comes just four months after the developer purchased a nearby, low-rise condo building for $45.5 million, which will likely be redeveloped. Earlier this month, up north in Fort Lauderdale, the firm bought an oceanfront hotel for $60 million. A representative for El-Ad Group was not immediately available for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialoserver.com.
bullets: Azora and Vizcaya Capital sold Grove at 3250 Mary, 80,000-sq-ft office in Coconut Grove, for $62.3M
1-year hold; purchased for $47.5M in Sept 2024; ~$15M gain on stabilized office asset
Buyer tied to Israeli billionaire Tshuva's El-Ad Group; reflects luxury real estate demand and supply scarcity
stories.summary: Azora Private Solutions and Vizcaya Capital sold the Grove at 3250 Mary, an 80,000-square-foot five-story office building in Miami's Coconut Grove neighborhood, for $62.3 million just over one year after acquiring it for $47.5 million in September 2024. The buyer is an entity affiliated with El-Ad National Properties (Israeli billionaire Isaac Tshuva's El-Ad Group). Brokers Berkadia's Omar Morales and Jaret Turkell noted Coconut Grove's distinction as a top South Florida market driven by luxury residential buyers and high-net-worth office users.
stories.impact: Not directly relevant to multifamily development. However, foreign capital's continued appetite for South Florida luxury real estate and the rapid office appreciation cycle signal underlying wealth concentration and real estate scarcity in premium Miami submarkets. This indicates strong adjacent multifamily demand in Coconut Grove and nearby high-net-worth residential zones (Brickell, Design District); developers should monitor absorption and rental rate momentum in luxury Class A multifamily in South Florida's prestige corridors.

stories.title: Affinius Capital Lends $177M for Multifamily Asset Buy in New Jersey, Yonkers
stories.excerpt: A joint venture between Lincoln Property Company, Saber-Hightower and Waterfall Asset Management has sealed $177.25 million of acquisition financing for the purchase of two multifamily properties in the New York metropolitan area, Commercial Observer has learned. Affinus Capital provided the debt package for the sponsorship’s purchase of the 262-unit Edgewater Harbor property in Edgewater, N.J., and the soon-to-be completed 147-unit Trilogy Lofts at Tuckahoe project in Yonkers, N.Y. The deal involved a $124 million loan for Edgewater Harbor and $53.4 million of acquisition debt for Trilogy Lofts. The joint venture of Lincoln Property Company, Saber-Hightower and Waterfall Asset Management acquired both properties from National Resources as part of a $450 million acquisition of four tri-state region properties encompassing more than 4 million square feet, CO previously first reported. “Edgewater and Trilogy Lofts represent a compelling opportunity to invest in high-quality, well-located multifamily assets in supply-constrained, transit-oriented submarkets with durable renter demand,” David Greenburg, managing director at Affinius Capital, said in a statement. “Waterfall Asset Management, Lincoln Property Company and Saber-Hightower bring institutional scale, local market expertise, and a proven track record of value-add execution that positions this portfolio for long-term performance.” Cushman & Wakefield negotiated the financing with a team consisting of John Alascio, Alex Hernandez, Brad Domenico, Chuck Kohaut and Mitch Rothstein. C&W also represented the seller in the acquisition with a Northeast capital markets team of Andy Merin, Frank DiTommaso and Ryan Dowd. Located at 45 River Road 6 miles from Midtown Manhattan, Edgewater Harbor features 60,500 square feet of retail space anchored by a Sprouts Farmers Market slated to open in 2027. Community amenities include fitness centers, rooftop decks, coworking space and an outdoor pool. Trilogy Lofts at 1 Sca
bullets: Lincoln Property, Saber-Hightower, Waterfall AM closed $177.25M acquisition financing via Affinius Capital
262-unit Edgewater Harbor (NJ) and 147-unit Trilogy Lofts (Yonkers) purchased from National Resources
Part of larger $450M four-property NJ/NY metro acquisition; supply-constrained, transit-oriented submarkets
stories.summary: A joint venture of Lincoln Property Company, Saber-Hightower, and Waterfall Asset Management secured $177.25 million in acquisition financing from Affinius Capital for the purchase of two multifamily properties: the 262-unit Edgewater Harbor in Edgewater, New Jersey ($124M loan) and the soon-to-be-completed 147-unit Trilogy Lofts in Yonkers, New York ($53.4M loan). Both were acquired from National Resources as part of a larger $450 million acquisition of four tri-state region properties totaling over 4 million square feet.
stories.impact: Multifamily capital remains strong and willing to finance high-quality, transit-oriented acquisitions in supply-constrained NJ/NY metro submarkets, particularly near completion. Edgewater (PATH-proximate) and Yonkers (Metro-North) benefit from NYC commuter demand and limited new supply. The $177M package signals lender confidence in near-term NOI stability and rent growth in the I-95 corridor. This validates continued acquisition momentum in the New York tri-state region and suggests tight supply will support sustained rental rate power.
